summary: The root W-D-D primarily signifies love, affection, and desire. It encompasses wishing for something to happen or for someone to be in a certain state. It can also denote a strong, enduring fondness.

headwords.gloss: I wish that such a thing may be; O thou visitor of the sick, inquiring respecting us, wishing that thou mayest see my graveclothes

parts.t: I wish that such a thing may be.
In the following saying of the poet,
O thou visitor of the sick, inquiring respecting us, wishing that thou mayest see my graveclothes
is lengthened for sake of the measure. (S, L.)

headwords.def: وُدٌّ : see 1, and وِدٌّ , and وَدٌّ . بِوُدِّى أَنْ يَكُونَ كَذَا I wish that such a thing may be. In the following saying of the poet, أَيُّهَا العَائِدُ المُسَائِلُ عَنَّا وَبِوُدِّيكَ لَوْ ثَرَى أَكْفَانِى [ O thou visitor of the sick, inquiring respecting us, wishing that thou mayest see my graveclothes ], the kesreh of the د is lengthened for sake of the measure. (S, L.)
